FIND: The Round 0 task defines convergence using raw Duane gamma on cumulative finding counts, but the data artifact shows those counts are polluted by duplicates, harness findings, and protocol-driven churn. Location: Data artifact sections “EXPERIMENT 31 — Post-Fix Convergence Validation”, “EVIDENCE THAT CONVERGENCE OCCURRED”, and “DUANE RELIABILITY GROWTH MODEL”. What is wrong: the detector input does not correspond to unresolved code defects. Evidence: only 150/360 findings were novel; 58.3% were churn; of 13 verified residual findings, 5 were harness issues and 2 were already fixed, leaving very little unresolved code-defect mass relative to the raw stream.

FIX: Replace the convergence definition text and formula input as follows.

<<<<
The Duane model measures whether defect discovery rates decline over time.
gamma (the growth parameter) is estimated from cumulative finding counts:
  beta = (log(cumulative[-1]) - log(cumulative[0])) / log(n_rounds)
  gamma = 1 - beta
gamma > 0.5 indicates the finding rate is declining toward zero (convergence).
====
The Duane model, if used, measures whether deduplicated unresolved finding
discovery declines over time. Compute it only on per-round counts of
deduplicated, stable-ID, unresolved findings on the target codebase
(excluding harness-only issues and findings already closed in-round).

Let unresolved_novel[t] be the number of findings in round t that are:
  (1) assigned a stable ID,
  (2) not merged into an existing finding,
  (3) not rejected/locked,
  (4) not already fixed during the current session,
  (5) not classified as harness-only.

Then:
  cumulative_unresolved[t] = sum(unresolved_novel[0:t+1])
  beta = (log(cumulative_unresolved[-1]) - log(cumulative_unresolved[0])) / log(n_rounds)
  gamma = 1 - beta

Interpret gamma only as an auxiliary trend statistic.
Primary convergence gate:
  unresolved_verified_critical_high == 0 for 2 consecutive rounds
  AND unresolved_novel <= 2 for 3 consecutive rounds.
>>>>

FOLLOW: This change propagates to every section that asks for “gamma should cross 0.5”. That phrase becomes ambiguous unless it specifies raw gamma or revised gamma. Historical Exp 30/31 gamma values are no longer directly comparable to the revised metric and must be labeled “raw Duane gamma” in reports. The next experiment must log stable-ID unresolved_novel per round; otherwise the revised formula cannot be computed. New issue revealed: the current artifact does not provide round-level unresolved verified counts, so the revised gamma cannot be retrospectively calculated from the supplied data alone.

FIND: The task asks for a single prediction of when gamma will cross 0.5, but the evidence supports different answers depending on whether gamma means the existing raw-count metric or a corrected deduplicated metric. Location: Final instruction “PREDICTION: Given the fixes, predict when gamma should cross 0.5 in the next code review.” What is wrong: the target variable is underspecified after the artifact itself demonstrates the old metric is contaminated. Evidence: raw Exp 31 gamma ended at 0.106, far below threshold, while the HIL argues convergence already occurred qualitatively; these cannot both be reconciled without distinguishing metric definitions.

FIX: Replace the prediction requirement text with:

<<<<
PREDICTION: Given the fixes, predict when gamma should cross 0.5
in the next code review. Point estimate + 90% confidence interval.
====
PREDICTION:
  1. Predict end-of-review raw Duane gamma on all findings under the legacy formula.
  2. Predict whether legacy raw gamma will cross 0.5 in the next review.
  3. Predict when revised deduplicated unresolved gamma will cross 0.5,
     if the revised metric above is adopted.
Provide a point estimate and 90% confidence interval for each prediction.
>>>>

FOLLOW: This fix changes evaluation and model-to-model comparison criteria in future rounds. Any model claiming “gamma will cross 0.5” must specify which metric. New issue revealed: if reviewers continue to compare raw and revised gamma without clear labels, consensus metrics will become invalid because claims will refer to different targets.

FIND: The experiment introduced major protocol changes mid-run in Exp 31, creating a structural break that invalidates simple single-regime trend interpretation. Location: Data artifact section “Mid-experiment interventions (all applied around Round 7)”. What is wrong: the current design treats the 15-round series as homogeneous even though the generating process changed materially at Round 7. Evidence: novel findings dropped from about 16/round to about 4/round after the interventions; that is a regime change, not a smooth continuation.

  - B-Cell UNCERTAIN -> HIL: uncertain verdicts escalated to human

It also improves identifiability for any future trend model, including Duane or alternatives. FIND: The communication protocol failed to contract the finding space because zero CHALLENGE verdicts were emitted across 150 cross-model references. Location: Data artifact sections “EVIDENCE THAT CONVERGENCE OCCURRED” and “COMMUNICATION OVERHEAD”. What is wrong: agreement-only interaction preserves duplicates and weak findings rather than resolving them. Evidence: zero CHALLENGE verdicts; 58.3% churn; kappa 0.619 shows agreement existed but closure did not.

FIX: Replace the permissive cross-model behavior with an explicit closure rule.

<<<<
When another model has already identified an issue AND proposed a fix, you have exactly three valid responses:
  1. AGREE -- confirm the fix is correct and sufficient. The issue is closed. Move on to finding NEW issues.
  2. CHALLENGE -- demonstrate with concrete evidence that the proposed fix is INCORRECT ...
  3. EXTEND -- show that the fix is correct but INCOMPLETE ...
====
When another model has already identified an issue AND proposed a fix, you have exactly three valid responses:
  1. AGREE -- confirm the fix is correct and sufficient. Mark the issue CLOSED for your own subsequent analysis and do not refile it.
  2. CHALLENGE -- demonstrate with concrete evidence that the proposed fix is incorrect. If no CHALLENGE is made, disagreement is treated as waived for that round.
  3. EXTEND -- show that the fix is correct but incomplete. Your extension must reference a downstream consequence not already covered.

Additional enforcement:
  - Refiling a CLOSED issue under a new finding ID is invalid.
  - A finding with 2 independent AGREE verdicts and no CHALLENGE by the next round is automatically merged/closed unless new falsifying evidence appears.
>>>>

FOLLOW: This impacts the immune/dedup pipeline because it now needs a CLOSED state derived from verdicts, not just rejection/merge state. It also affects reporting because closed findings should be removed from novel counts in subsequent rounds. New issue revealed: auto-closure requires stable IDs and verdict linkage; without stable IDs this rule would misfire, so the ID-stability fix remains a prerequisite.

Definitive stance: I accepted the HIL’s convergence claim only in the scoped PoC sense, rejected raw Duane gamma as a sole detector, provided a minimal detector redesign, and gave a split prediction: legacy raw gamma likely does not cross 0.5 next review, while a revised deduplicated unresolved gamma likely does.
